stem:
A 21-year-old college student presents to the office due to intense itching that is worse at night.  Several roommates have similar symptoms.  Physical examination shows:

  • Excoriated papules in the finger webs and on the wrists
  • Thin, serpiginous burrows in several interdigital spaces

What is the most appropriate treatment?​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​​​​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​
explanation:
This patient with interdigital burrows and intense nocturnal itching most likely has scabies.  Scabies is a contagious skin infestation caused by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei and commonly spreads through prolonged skin-to-skin contact (eg, among household members or roommates).

After transmission, the mites enter the superficial epidermis, where female mites create burrows and deposit eggs and fecal material.  A delayed hypersensitivity reaction to the mites and their products causes intense pruritus, which is characteristically worse at night.  Typical findings include excoriated papules and thin, serpiginous burrows involving the finger webs, wrists, waist, and genitals.

First-line treatment is topical permethrin cream, which is applied to the entire body from the neck down and then washed off after several hours, with treatment generally repeated after 7 days.  Close contacts should be treated simultaneously, and recently used clothing and bedding should be washed or isolated to prevent reinfestation.  Oral ivermectin is also effective but is preferred for crusted scabies (ie, extensive hyperkeratotic plaques with a high mite burden) or when topical therapy is impractical or unsuccessful.

(Choice A)  Albendazole treats cutaneous larva migrans (eg, Ancylostoma braziliense), which causes pruritic, migrating serpiginous tracks, typically on the feet after exposure to contaminated soil.  Interdigital burrows and widespread nocturnal pruritus is most consistent with scabies.

(Choice C)  Prednisone can suppress inflammation and pruritus in inflammatory skin disorders (eg, severe allergic contact dermatitis).  However, immunosuppression does not eradicate scabies and can allow the infestation to worsen.

(Choice D)  Terbinafine is an antifungal medication used for dermatophyte infections (eg, tinea corporis), which typically cause annular, scaly plaques rather than nocturnal pruritus with interdigital burrows.

(Choice E)  Valacyclovir is used for herpesvirus infections (eg, herpes zoster), which typically cause painful grouped vesicles in a dermatomal distribution.

Educational objective:Scabies causes intense nocturnal pruritus with papules and characteristic serpiginous burrows, particularly in the finger webs and on the wrists.  First-line treatment of uncomplicated scabies is topical permethrin cream; close contacts should be treated simultaneously to prevent reinfestation.​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌​​​​​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​
